title: Canonical output enforcement: validation matrix and streaming-toolcall compatibility
creator: Priya Desai
description: Goal: Create a comprehensive validation matrix and test harness that verifies strict structured-output enforcement across streaming responses and tool/function-calling flows. This ticket covers test design, CI integration, flaky-case mitigation strategies, and runbook for fallbacks when strict enforcement conflicts with streaming partials or toolcall interleaving. We must ensure that constrained-decoding heuristics, sentinel markers, and lightweight reparsing strategies produce deterministic validation outcomes and clear developer-facing error signals.
acceptance_criteria: Matrix enumerates at least 30 combinations of streaming chunk boundaries, toolcall insertion points, and partial-token cutoffs
CI job added that runs the matrix nightly with pass/fail reporting to the console dashboard
Regression thresholds: <3% transient flakiness after heuristics; <0.5% uncovered schema violations for canonical models
Runbook documented for when streaming partials break schema enforcement (link to runbook in attachments)
PR with implementation and tests merged and linked in comments
testing_plan: Create synthetic request batches that exercise: single-object streams, multi-object streams, early toolcall delimiter insertion, and KV-cache-mispredict sequences
Injection tests where model emits a valid schema but with extra non-JSON tokens before/after (e.g., narrative prefix/suffix)
Streaming-truncation recovery tests that simulate client disconnects and server retries; verify decoder recovers or fails gracefully
Tool/function calling interop tests: tool returns plain text, tool returns JSON blob, tool returns chunked output mid-stream; validate final merged output against schema
Constrained decoding fuzz tests that enforce token-set whitelists for structural tokens (braces, separators) and measure false-positive rejection rates
Compare strict mode vs. lenient-with-repair mode: record repair attempts and resulting semantic fidelity using existing eval prompts
notes: Design trade-offs: strict enforcement yields early errors but can break streaming UX; repair heuristics can mask model issues and hide upstream regressions.
We will prefer deterministic, reproducible repair steps (truncate trailing partial token, apply single-pass reparse with sentinel) rather than stochastic sampling-based fixes.
Plan acknowledges existing console UX: surface non-fatal schema repairs as warnings with opt-out flags for customers who require absolute fidelity.
Cross-team reviews requested: API (for default error semantics), Console (for new warning surfaces), and Docs (examples for developers on how to opt into lenient modes)
implementation_steps: Draft matrix spreadsheet and commit to repo under tests/structured_output/matrix.csv
Implement harness that can replay recorded streaming token sequences and inject toolcall boundaries
Add constrained-decoder shim that can be toggled per-test and instrument token-level decisions
Create CI pipeline step that runs the matrix and uploads a compressed artifact with failing traces
Wire nightly job into Console dashboard with pass/fail and flaky-test tagging
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Matrix test runtime could be long. Mitigation: use sampling strategy for CI (nightly full run, patch-trigger quick subset)
Risk: Repair heuristics may produce incorrect user-visible output. Mitigation: require repair logs and checksum of original output for audit until repair is GA
Risk: Tool-call interleaving complexity. Mitigation: start with canonical toolcall markers and one-off tool response shapes before expanding to arbitrary tool chains
